content: Always consult your healthcare professional for comprehensive information about this medication and your specific health needs. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, or headache. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacterium called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has ended. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, also contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before using oritavancin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Share your complete medical history with your doctor or pharmacist before using this medication. Oritavancin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as blood clotting tests (e.g., PT/INR/aPTT), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., liver function tests) may be conducted while you are using this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. Storage: Not applicable. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
